meta.title: Kinderszenen Op. 15 No. 10 'Fast zu ernst' (annotated)
meta.notation_notes: D#4 pickup checked at absolute quarter 867.75; bar 1 at 868. No. 11 starts at 928, in G. The supplied performance unfolds the 13-bar phrase twice (second statement starts at 894), followed by bars 27–28 and a 4/4 closing bar at 924. The MIDI key signature B is interpreted as G# minor, with E# and Fx spelled correctly. No score repeats are added. The empty end of the final 4/4 bar is retained.

loop_candidates.why: D# pickup plus 13-bar loop, per note recurrence; end at 893.75, moving the returning pickup to the seam.

hook_candidates.why: Delayed upper G#–B–A# against G# and Fx bass motion.
A#7 → D#m, then D#7 → G#m creates the dark turn and return.

kpop_uses.why: The displaced melody and broad bass leave a restrained narrative groove.
A#7 → D# minor detour can build tension before a return to G# minor.
Use the full asymmetric phrase as an instrumental bridge; keep its 13-bar length.
Revoice the closing G# minor arrival as a sustained refrain; no literal final-chorus step-up occurs.

review_flags.reason: Bar 10 diminished colour retains D-natural; interpretation above the D# pedal is uncertain. Check against a critical edition.
Loop seam uses abs 893.75 (26 quarters), not full downbeat 894; move the pickup deliberately when arranging.

summary: A displaced sixteenth-note song whose 13-bar span is part of the tension. The tune moves through B major and D# minor without losing the gravity of G# minor. The repeat is already written out in this MIDI; the final open fifth is a tonic ending but cannot pass a full triad check.
tricks: The melody begins at beat 1.25 while the low bass attacks on beat 1: preserve this built-in hesitation.
The 13-bar phrase closes through the relative major and a D# dominant; a conventional 12-bar crop loses its own restart.
Low bass, broken inner notes and upper tune form distinct layers; the source MIDI is insufficient to claim canon or invertible counterpoint.
